llmlang.lockfile_builder.finalize.disposition: fixed a real misuse of 'accepts': a bullet describing what a fresh manifest value can look like ('accepts a fresh disposition in the manifest as a plain string...') reused the word reserved for the entry's own §4b bookend, giving this entry two 'accepts' bullets with no clear reason. Restructured the whole disposition-resolution walk condition-first per §4c (checks whether the key still names a current entry; for a fresh-value case, stamps it; for an already-stamped case, keeps-or-drops it) instead of describing it as a loose sequence of facts. Also repositioned the 'builds every hash and disposition fresh...' # commentary to sit right before the closing writes/returns bullets, matching build()'s own layout - it's a global property of the whole computation, not anchored to the specific bullet it used to sit next to. No behavior changed.

llmlang.cli.run_check.disposition: fixed the same 'accepts' misuse: a bullet describing path auto-discovery reused the word reserved for the entry's own bookend. Reworded to state the real behavior (discovers vs. checks-directly) without the word 'accepts'. No behavior changed.
